activity.notes: David IV the Builder was enthroned as king of the united Kingdom of Georgia in 1089 after the removal/abdication of his father Giorgi II and remained king until his death on 24 January 1125. Georgian reference works consistently give the reign as 1089-1125, while the Georgian Encyclopedia supplies the exact death date. ATLAS therefore stores a single continuous sovereign reign. His territorial expansion, reconquest of Tbilisi in 1122, and wider Caucasian supremacy did not create a separate polity identity or interrupt his underlying kingship of Georgia.

sources.title: დავით IV აღმაშენებელი
sources.citation_text: The Georgian Encyclopedia identifies David IV Aghmashenebeli as king of Georgia from 1089 to 1125 and gives his death as 24 January 1125.

sources.title: coin - Davit IV
sources.citation_text: The British Museum identifies Davit IV as the ruler represented on a Georgian royal coin and dates his authority to 1089-1125; the inscription calls him King David and lists the peoples and lands under his rule.

sources.title: King David IV - The Builder
sources.citation_text: The British Council in Georgia states that King David IV of Georgia was crowned in 1089 after his father Giorgi II abdicated and describes his 36-year reign and unification of the Georgian state.

sources.title: დავით აღმაშენებლის ძეგლი
sources.citation_text: The National Parliamentary Library of Georgia identifies David IV the Builder as king of Georgia from 1089 to 1125 and a member of the Bagrationi dynasty.
